podcast.title: Conception of Kiss's Makeup
podcast.body: Paul Stanley revealed that Kiss's iconic makeup was designed as a collective effort, allowing each band member to develop a unique character that symbolized and embodied them as individuals. He emphasized the "synergy" involved in creating these distinct visual identities. "the makeup seemed like the perfect way for each one of us to come up with a character that symbolized and embodied us as individuals."

podcast.title: Martian Crater
podcast.body: Paul Stanley of Kiss has a Martian crater named after him, an unusual distinction given that typically craters on Mars are named after deceased scientists and writers who contributed to Mars study and lore, and Stanley is neither deceased nor a scientist. "Paul Stanley of Kiss has a Martian crater named after him, but notice that he's neither dead nor a scientist nor anyone who has really anything to do with Mars."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Theatrical Guitar Smashing
podcast.body: During KISS's performances in the 1970s, Paul Stanley would theatrically destroy numerous guitars as a regular component of the band's live show, enhancing their visual spectacle. "Paul Stanley, theatrically, went through many, many guitars as part of his show."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
